title: SDK Integration Walkthrough - AstraCommerce
summary: Initial SDK integration walkthrough for AstraCommerce focused on Python/TypeScript quickstarts, auth options (API keys, service accounts, SSO), environment setup, and next steps for a pilot. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, performance and latency targets, security/compliance needs, and benchmark plan.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendes (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Sophie Turner (AstraCommerce - Head of ML); Mark Liu (AstraCommerce - Staff Engineer); Jamal Brown (AstraCommerce - CTO)

Summary (auto): quick SDK walkthrough, auth & env setup, demo of Python + TS snippets, discuss dedicated/private options and next steps for pilot.

[00:00:05] Carlos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Carlos from Redwood, and with me is Priya who'll walk through the SDK and some integration patterns. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:14] Sophie: Doing great, thanks. Excited to see the quickstarts — we want a straightforward way to get embeddings and chat generation into our checkout assistant.
[00:00:23] Mark: Yeah, and also curious about auth and secrets management — our infra is pretty locked down.
[00:00:28] Priya: Totally, we'll cover auth up front. We'll show both Python and TypeScript flows, env var setup, and then demo streaming and embeddings. Quick note: some of the transcript may have small transcribe hiccups, apologies in advance.

[00:01:10] Priya: Ok jumping in — for Python the basic install is pip install redwood-inference (or the short package redwood-sdk), then set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-... For TS/NPM it's npm i @redwood/inference and you set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or use a .env file.
[00:01:44] Mark: Are there service account tokens or SSO options? We don't want developers embedding org keys.
[00:01:51] Carlos: Yes, good call. We support per-service tokens that you can mint via the Console, and for enterprise customers you can connect SAML/SSO to manage RBAC. We can provision a read-only service account for embeddings and a separate production key for generation.
[00:02:08] Sophie: How do you rotate keys and connect to our KMS? We use AWS KMS and have strict audit requirements.
[00:02:15] Priya: Platform integrates with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration and audit logs. Key rotation can be automated via the Console or using the API — we'll send the exact steps in the security docs pack.

[00:03:05] Priya: Live code: Python snippet for text generation. from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) ; resp = client.generate(model="redwood-3b", prompt="Hello, world", max_tokens=64) — response streaming is supported with client.stream_generate(...) and you'll get chunked events for UI updates.
[00:03:42] Mark: Model names — will you provide a curated model catalog and compatibility guarantees? We need predictable p95 latencies.
[00:03:50] Carlos: Yep, the Console shows verified performance profiles and you can pin model variants. For strict SLA we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted we publish performance profiles and typical p95 numbers per model.

[00:04:30] Priya: On embeddings: batch embeddings via client.embed_batch([...]) to amortize costs. We also support synchronous and async jobs; for large backfills we recommend the async job API to avoid client timeouts.
[00:04:55] Sophie: Can you do batching automatically? Our traffic pattern is bursty at checkout.
[00:05:02] Priya: The SDK supports a background batcher plus we have server-side intelligent batching and KV cache for prefix hits. You can tune batch windows in the client SDK or rely on server batching for lower latency/cost tradeoffs.

[00:06:10] Carlos: A few common enterprise asks — audit logs, SSO, network controls like IP allowlists and VPC peering, and data residency. We can cover each; which are must-haves for you?
[00:06:24] Jamal: Audit logs and VPC are musts, plus SOC2 type 2 evidence. We're evaluating Private deployment for PCI-scope data.
[00:06:33] Carlos: Understood. Private supports customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging; we'll attach the SOC2 and ISO docs.

[00:07:10] Priya: Back to SDK quickstart — TypeScript example: import {Redwood} from "@redwood/inference"; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: "redwood-chat-3b", messages: [{role:"user", content:"Summarize order 123"}] }); // stream with client.chat.stream(...)
[00:07:45] Mark: For streaming in the browser, do you recommend direct calls from frontend or via a backend proxy? We want to hide keys and enforce rate limits.
[00:07:53] Priya: Backend proxy is recommended. Use short-lived signed tokens for the browser if you need direct streaming; otherwise proxy through your API gateway so you can apply auth and quotas.

[00:08:30] Sophie: Any gotchas on WebSocket streaming vs SSE?
[00:08:34] Priya: We support both patterns; SSE works fine for many dashboards. WebSocket is lower overhead for persistent streams. We'll share examples for both in the quickstart repo.

[00:09:10] Carlos: Let's talk telemetry — cost and latency breakdowns appear in the Console. You can see token-level costs, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks to tie requests back to users.
[00:09:25] Jamal: Important — can we tag traffic by team or customer id? We have per-tenant billing needs.
[00:09:30] Priya: Yes, tags/metadata on requests are supported and appear in logs and cost reports. You can pass a metadata object with every request.

[00:10:20] Mark: About performance: we have a p95 target of 250ms for assistant responses under normal load. What can we expect on hosted?
[00:10:28] Carlos: For smaller models and optimized request paths we often hit <200ms p95 for short prompts; larger models will be higher. If you need strict 250ms under load, Dedicated with appropriate GPU profile is more reliable. We can run a benchmark with your representative prompts.

[00:11:05] Priya: I'll demo a simple end-to-end: local env, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run python quickstart which calls embed->index->search->generate. (typing noises) Here's a small example showing how we persist embeddings to your vector store; we support offthe-shelf connectors and you can upload to Pinecone, Milvus, or your own vector DB.
[00:11:45] Sophie: We currently use a hosted vector DB (managed) but might move to self-hosted; is there any lock-in?
[00:11:52] Priya: No vendor lock-in; the SDK returns embeddings and you can store wherever you like. We also support server-side caching and prefix KV cache to speed up repeated prompts. Note: some transcripts show KV cash, that's just a transcribe typo.

[00:13:00] Carlos: Security review — we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, customer KMS for encryption at rest. If you need an on-prem package, there's a private deployment with a customer-managed control plane.
[00:13:20] Jamal: Any E2E encryption for in-flight data beyond TLS?
[00:13:26] Priya: TLS is standard; for extra controls Private deployment gives you network isolation. We can discuss tunnel or on-prem proxy for additional encryption layers if required.

[00:14:15] Mark: CI/CD integration — how to rotate service tokens in our pipelines?
[00:14:21] Carlos: Use the Console to create short-lived tokens and inject via your secret manager (Vault/Secrets Manager). We have an API to rotate keys programmatically; we'll include scripts in the repo.

[00:15:10] Sophie: Can we test model regression? We want monitors tied to our prompt sets.
[00:15:15] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitors and regression alerts; you can bind evals to prompt suites and get alerts on distribution shifts or metric drops. We'll demo that separately.

[00:16:00] Priya: Ok quick live demo of TypeScript quickstart — creating a chat session, calling function/tool calling example: you can define functions in the request and get structured returns. Sample code in repo: functionSpec: { name: "getOrder", params: { orderId: "string" } } and then the model will call it.
[00:16:38] Mark: Tool calling reliability is important; how deterministic are the calls?
[00:16:42] Priya: It's as deterministic as the underlying model; we recommend synthetic tests and function schemas. Redwood also supports function calling hints and a verification hook.

[00:17:30] Carlos: Pricing note — hosted pricing is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit. We'll send the dedicated workbook after this call.
[00:17:45] Jamal: Any discounts for multi-year or committed capacity?
[00:17:48] Carlos: Yes, typical enterprise discounts for annual commitments. We'll include an initial pricing sheet with the proposal.

[00:18:30] Priya: Demo wrap-up — code snippets, quickstarts, and security FAQs are in the repo link I'll share. Example quick commands: pip install redwood-inference; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; python examples/generate.py. For TS: npm i @redwood/inference; node examples/stream.js.

[00:19:05] Sophie: Can you assume we need PCI scope isolation? If so, timeline for Private trial?
[00:19:12] Carlos: We can provision Private trial lanes; timeline depends on procurement but typical pilot is 2-4 weeks for an eval environment. We'll pair SE to run benchmarks.

[00:20:00] Priya: Technical detail: for low latency we do compiled kernels, quantization options, and KV cache. If you want smaller memory footprint on Dedicated we recommend INT8 quantized variants which reduce cost but you should test for any quality regressions.
[00:20:30] Mark: Are those quantized models served transparently or do we need model changes?
[00:20:34] Priya: Served as compatible variants; the API model name will reflect quantization (eg redwood-3b-int8). You can pin the variant or use routing policies.

[00:21:20] Carlos: Next — integrations with our observability: tracing headers include request-id and route; you can correlate with your tracing system.
[00:21:31] Sophie: Perfect, that's a requirement.

[00:22:10] Priya: I'm going to run a short embedding batch to show throughput. (brief pause, typing) The SDK will chunk and the server will return batch ids — you can poll or receive webhooks. We'll share the webhook schema.

[00:23:20] Carlos: Ok let's cover the pilot scope: we propose a 2-week pilot focusing on checkout assistant — ingest 100k past queries, run embeddings, and measure p95 and cost. We will run benchmark with your prompts. Does that sound right?
[00:23:36] Jamal: Yes that sounds reasonable. Budget we can commit to small pilot but need clear success criteria.
[00:23:42] Sophie: Success criteria: p95 < 250ms for generation, similarity recall > 92% on our test set, and acceptable cost per 1k queries.

[00:24:05] Priya: Great. We'll draft a pilot plan with milestones and measurement plan.

[00:24:45] Mark: A few random questions — SDK license? OSS?
[00:24:50] Carlos: The SDK has an Apache-style permissive license for client libs and the quickstarts are open. Server components vary by deployment type. We'll include license details in the repo.

[00:25:30] Sophie: Can you share a sample quickstart repo link now?
[00:25:34] Priya: I'll drop it in chat after — github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: placeholder link, will share exact repo).

[00:26:10] Carlos: Wrapping up — any blockers from your side for starting the pilot?
[00:26:16] Jamal: Procurement will need SOC2, contract T&Cs; security will need the KMS and VPC docs.
[00:26:24] Carlos: We'll send the security pack and SOC2, and loop in our solutions engineer for deployment details.

[00:27:05] Priya: One last demo note — error handling patterns in the SDK: exponential backoff for 5xx, deterministic retry for idempotent endpoints, and guidance for streaming reconnects. We'll add examples to README.
[00:27:30] Mark: Great.

[00:28:00] Carlos: Ok let's do a quick recap of action items and next steps.
[00:28:05] Sophie: Perfect.

[00:28:10] Carlos: Actions: we'll send pilot proposal, send pricing/dedicated workbook, security docs, quickstart repo, and schedule a follow-up benchmark run with Priya.
[00:28:25] Jamal: Who will be the main point of contact?
[00:28:28] Carlos: I'll be the AE contact for procurement and Priya will run the technical bench and onboarding.

[00:29:00] Priya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a benchmarking session and a short checklist of data needed.
[00:29:10] Sophie: Sounds good.

[00:30:00] Carlos: Thanks everyone. We'll drop all the materials and follow up on next steps.
[00:30:08] Mark: Thanks.
[00:30:12] Jamal: Appreciate it.

(Transcript continues with short clarifications and outro; remaining time used for brief Q&A and scheduling)
